name: Nethaniah
overview: Nethaniah is a male biblical figure known primarily as the son of Shelemiah, as recorded in Jeremiah 36:14. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him in Scripture. His mention is brief, focusing on his familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethaniah means 'YHWH has given,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's provision. This name is a proper name and is not indicated as being given directly by God in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Nethaniah as the son of Shelemiah and infers that he is the father of Jehudi. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Nethaniah's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his family lineage, particularly as the son of Shelemiah and the father of Jehudi. His mention in Jeremiah 36:14 places him within the context of the prophet Jeremiah's ministry and the unfolding events during that time. Though his role is not elaborated, his connection to Jehudi, who is known in the narrative, highlights his place within the historical setting of Judah's prophetic history.
